data.why: these loops already use native capsule queries and packed-position prefilters; the remaining cost is reading entity Dictionaries per candidate, which native code reads no faster (native prep_units_ids pays ~1.9 us/unit). data.proposed: Same look, far fewer canvas commands. (1) Put all ring segments and arrow shafts in one antialiased draw_multiline_colors call and all arrow heads in one RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_triangle_array call. If segment joints look different at alpha below 1, build the ring bands as one triangle mesh with a 1 px feather instead (what an AA polyline does internally). (2) Rebuild that geometry only when _threats or _waves change (the 6 Hz dot rebuild) and animate the pulse through a time uniform or a modulate on a child CanvasItem, instead of re-issuing about 70 commands every frame. Expected: about 110 fewer draw calls per frame at 10k, putting g71 back at the g7 level there.

api.register: static RenderSnap.register_g71(key: String, provider: Callable) -> void  (re-registering a key replaces it)
api.unregister: static RenderSnap.unregister_g71(key: String) -> void (unknown key = no-op)
api.provider: provider.call(w, snap) -> Variant, called once per snapshot build, after every built-in field is in snap (ids/pos/flags final: align packed arrays with snap.ids), in registration order; return stored at snap.g71[key]
api.empty: no provider registered = no loop, no snap.g71 key, sim hash unchanged (render_snap is view-side)

data.rules: register once at load/setup on the main thread, never while a step is in flight (register swaps in a new dict, so a build in flight keeps the old one); providers only READ w (no sim writes, no rng), run on the sim worker thread (no nodes), return fresh or copy-on-write data (packed arrays, small dicts), never a live entity dict

data.why: Setup bug that A5 exposed, not a speed bug. The parked CN soldier (id 987) is KILLED during the 60x4-tick loop, so w.entities[parked] at line 324 errors. Every point of damage on him is his own side's fire at the m_walker placed 1 tile west of him (cn_popup facility turret splash ~190, Sentinel marksman/bulwark/arc strays 40-83); the walker itself never hits him. Whether he lives is luck: in G7 the Sentinel harpoon (shooter 966) one-shots the walker at tick 146 (2325 dmg) and nothing fires near him; in HEAD the same shot misses because A5 moved every unit during the 25-tick _lp warm-up and the 6 s run (different positions, different rolls). With the setup shifted by 0/1/2/3/4/8 ticks, G7 also kills him once (shift 2, died tick 217: cn_popup 194 + sent_marksman 80) and HEAD twice (shift 0, 3). HEAD with all unit speeds divided by 1.2 reproduces G7 exactly (walker killed at 146, no damage), so A5 is the only trigger. The test's claim (a parked soldier holds and never walks toward the enemy) does not need him alive for 12 s: stop sampling when he dies and judge the hold on his last state. The 'fired' check at line 330 still sees target == near_foe (HEAD k=0: target 1000). Alternative if the owner prefers: keep the loop and make the in-range foe one the base cannot splash him with, but that changes the scenario more.

Sailing the lane x=45.5 the 4 mines are in reach for y in [48.2, 54.8] (6.6 tiles). G7 (3.4 t/s): 8 passes in reach, clears at y 49.3 / 51.0 / 52.7 / 54.4 (last with 0.36 tiles to spare) -> 4/4. A5 (4.08 t/s): 7 passes, clears at 49.7 / 51.7 / 53.8, the next pass is at y 55.2, out of reach -> 3/4, one mine left (trace .plan/speedfix71/probe_sweep.gd). The rule works as specified (2 mines/s while in reach; detection, no trigger, no damage all unchanged); the one-pass-clears-all expectation is speed-coupled with no margin. Fix: end the move on the far edge of the field (y 54.5, both far mines within 2.24) so the sweeper finishes the lane; the loop already waits for cleared >= 4 and not moving. Owner alternative (balance, not a bug): a sweeper budget per tile sailed or sweep_mines_per_s x g71_speed_mult in content/g6/rules_naval.json, which would keep one-pass clearing at A5 speed.

data.why: Not a sim fault and not an alarm: fails {} and no threat in all trees. The per-face count gives each man the face his position is nearest to, ties to the first face (N before W). The W wall run (S7._wall_routes route 2) ends ON the NW corner waypoint (21,21); a pair pauses there 2-10 s. Patrol arrival is checked once per think (1 s) within arrive 1.4: at G7 speed the W-run warden 185 is caught 0.47 short and pauses at (21.00,21.47) (1277 paused ticks; marksman 186 at (21.45,22.25)) = face W. With A5 (x1.2) men step past the 1.4 window between thinks and walk onto the waypoint: 185 pauses at (21.00,21.00) 608 ticks, 186 at (21.45,21.45) = an exact N/W tie -> counted N. Every live W dip (t=2850, 3450, 3500, 3550, 4100; W=5) is exactly the wall:2:1 pair standing on that corner; the other 5 (W towers 46/47/48 + wall:2:0 pair) are on W. The fix counts a wall-run man who is on his own run (the test's own on-run rule, _route_d <= 1.6, line 788) for his run's face (nearest face to the run's middle waypoint); everyone else keeps the nearest-face rule. Not a weakening: means are unchanged (W 7.1 vs 7.2/7.3 before), the bar stays >= 6, corner towers are not double counted (a both-faces tie rule was tried and rejected: W min 9, inflated). With the fix all three trees give the same per-face minimum [9,8,8,7] (N,E,S,W), i.e. the check no longer depends on where on the corner a patrol happens to stop.

data.measured: probe .plan/fires71/probe_reach.gd, log .plan/fires71/reach_raw.log, seed 4242 after the facility fill (tick 15, build_g71_late). Strips: 4 faces, each a 61-tile line 40.5 tiles from the base centre. Our indirect guns: 25 (18 G7 howitzer pits range 20, a_mlrs range 22, 2 a_sp_howitzer range 20, 2 base a_g71_mlrs range 22, 2 ARMY71 a_g71_grenadier counted as mortars range 7). Reaching a strip centre (range + 1 slack): 8 of 25. Per face: east face 0 = 5 guns (3 pits at x109, a_mlrs, base mlrs 1268); south face 1 = 1 (pit 691); west face 2 = 1 (base mlrs 1267, 21.4 vs 23); north face 3 = 1 (pit 677). The 6 corner pits sit 38.9 tiles out but 29-33 tiles from the nearest strip centre (12.6-14.1 tiles from a strip END: they could cover the strip ends only). The 2 base MLRS on the core ring (~21 tiles from centre) each reach exactly one face, at the edge of range. The 2 SP howitzers reach none (22.7 / 28.7).
options: A (recommended, no rule change): the LP base file places fire-support guns near the faces: e.g. near=outer_ring for the 2 MLRS + 1 mortar team per face 6-10 tiles inside each wall, so every face gets >= 3 guns in reach. Only content/g71_lp/lp_base_fires.json changes (my file); LP hashes move again, LP tests rerun.

B: an FPF-only reach rule: guns within range + fpf_reach_bonus (e.g. +12 tiles, PROVISIONAL) of a strip may join FPF, so the corner and inner pits answer every adjacent face. Simple, but it is a range the guns do not have for any other mission.

C: strips closer in: put the default strip 30 m out from the wall instead of the current offset (owner said 30-60 m), moving every strip ~6-10 tiles toward the centre; more pits reach, the strips also sit closer to our own walls (more danger-close).
